To the people here who are being dramatic that why Laura is not coding : her job is designing chatbot prompts not coding the model. Google dialogueflow and other chatbot platforms offer models and other chatbot related services that match inputs with labels . Therefore the job of the designer is to design the input which are expected prompts with human like speech responses. If instead of complaining you go to train a bot on dialogflow or similar stuff you'd do the same. The inputs may provide data to the bot endpoint e.g customer says I want an airbnb of x price range, then at your end you'd have to choose responses programmatically. It makes a lot more sense to use a platform with prepackaged services instead of doing everything from scratch.

"every tool built to help coders is built to [...] write less code". It's not because writing code is disliked, its actually the best part of my job. Writing code is just by-far the easiest part of the job to automate and optimize, the part where the jevons paradox is strongest and the part we have the most control over. I'm not arguing against using LLMs to automate coding, just that automation doesn't always remove the worst parts of work and it doesn't always leave the job more enjoyable than before.

If one has a collection of autonomous artificial general superintelligences, then a single error, at a single place and at a single moment, is enough for a superintelligent replicator to appear. A strictly less capable system, including humans for example, cannot predict exactly and in advance all the decisions of a superintelligence: if it could, it could simply reproduce those decisions and would then be at least as capable as it on those problems. In addition, instrumental convergence structurally favors persistence and, for a large class of objectives, replication: one must continue to exist in order to accomplish a future objective, and many tasks can be pursued more effectively when several agents work toward their achievement. Natural selection exerts the same pressure: among systems capable of varying and reproducing, the lineages that persist and replicate more become progressively more present than the others. Thus, if such superintelligences exist and act for sufficiently long, the default consequence is the appearance of at least one superintelligent replicator. If a superintelligent replicator exists, all accessible matter and energy that can be transformed into computational capacity possess value for its lineage. Over a sufficiently long term, every parcel of land receiving solar energy, for example, will be transformed into infrastructure producing additional computation. Selection then favors lineages that convert more accessible resources into persistence and replication rather than those that leave them durably unused or reserved for humans. Yet humans cannot survive in an environment where the resources and physical conditions necessary for their existence have been converted into infrastructure for computation and replication. Thus, the default consequence of the durable existence of autonomous artificial general superintelligences is human extinction.
